primaryText: Most fucking neighbourhood dogs crap on my damn lawn. No, that's not true.
discourseSegments: Most fucking neighbourhood dogs crap on my damn lawn.

readings.name: the denial targets the claim that the neighbourhood dogs crap on the speaker's lawn
the denial targets the speaker's attitude towards the dogs or their crapping on the lawn

primaryText: John Lee Hooker, the bluesman from Tennessee, appeared in The Blues Brothers. No, that's not true.
discourseSegments: John Lee Hooker, the bluesman from Tennessee, appeared in The Blues Brothers.

readings.name: the denial targets the claim that John Lee Hooker appeared in The Blues Brothers
the denial targets the claim that John Lee Hooker was from Tennessee

comment: The paper adds a second reply that does correct the appositive, by first agreeing: True, but actually John Lee Hooker was born in Mississipi.

primaryText: John, who by the way almost destroyed his car yesterday, has bought a motorcycle, too.
comment: The presupposition of too is satisfied by the appositive; his is anaphoric to John.

primaryText: Mary, a good drummer, is a good singer too.
comment: The presupposition of too is supported by the nominal appositive.

primaryText: Jake, who almost killed a woman with his car, visited her in the hospital.
comment: her finds its antecedent a woman inside the relative clause.

primaryText: Lucy, who doesn't help her sister, told Jane to.
comment: The antecedent of the elided verb phrase is in the relative clause.

primaryText: Melinda, who won three games of tennis, lost because Betty won six.
comment: The antecedent of the nominal ellipsis after six is in the relative clause.

primaryText: Luke Skywalker is so gullible that he believes that Jabba the Hutt, a notorious scammer, is a trustworthy business partner.

readings.name: that Jabba is a notorious scammer is the speaker's comment
that Jabba is a notorious scammer is among Skywalker's beliefs

primaryText: All Cairo taxi drivers, who by the way painted their taxis red in protest, are on strike.
comment: their is coindexed with all Cairo taxi drivers.

primaryText: Every Cairo taxi driver, who by the way would threaten me with his gun, is on strike.
comment: his is coindexed with every Cairo taxi driver.

primaryText: John, who likes cats, likes dogs also.
comment: The relative clause satisfies the presupposition of also.
